key_insight: Brain-Adapter combines text-guided and visual multiple-instance learning to improve scan-level diagnosis of 3D brain CT scans without dense annotations.
clinical_relevance: It could make acute intracranial pathology screening more scalable and clinically practical by using routine CT scans and reports to classify multiple findings at once.
method: Text-Conditioned Attention uses diagnostic sentences as semantic queries to align image regions with disease concepts.
A parallel visual MIL stream learns global scan-level features from structured labels extracted by an LLM.
An uncertainty-aware refinement module fuses both streams to improve ambiguous predictions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments showing Brain-Adapter outperformed state-of-the-art 3D models and standard MIL approaches on scan-level multi-label classification.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of report-derived labels and text-image alignment, so real-world deployment may be sensitive to noisy reports or domain shift.
paper_title: Brain-Adapter: A Dual-Stream Vision-Language MIL Framework for Comprehensive 3D CT Diagnosis of Acute Intracranial Pathologies
